name: Hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome
definition: Heritable connective-tissue disorder characterized by generalized joint hypermobility, instability, soft-tissue symptoms and characteristic systemic features, diagnosed clinically after exclusion of alternatives.

investigations.principle: No single confirmatory genetic test exists for hEDS; testing is directed at alternative genetic disorders when suspected.
investigations.MRI: Use MRI when neural, soft-tissue, labral, tendon, ligament, infection, occult injury or other condition-specific assessment requires it.
investigations.radiographs: Use radiographs and/or CT according to the condition-specific diagnostic pathway.

amber: High-velocity manipulation and unnecessary invasive procedures should be approached cautiously when significant instability exists.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Sandhi-asthirata/Dhatu-daurbalya phenotype may be documented only in parallel.

patientEducation.summary: Heritable connective-tissue disorder characterized by generalized joint hypermobility, instability, soft-tissue symptoms and characteristic systemic features, diagnosed clinically after exclusion of alternatives.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute neurovascular compromise, major trauma, rapidly progressive weakness, suspected serious infection, airway/vascular symptoms, unreduced dislocation or other listed red flags.
